clinician.trajectory_summary: An 83-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation (off rivaroxaban for 1 day prior to planned cataract surgery) presented as a stroke alert with nausea, dry mouth, left-sided tingling, and mild dysarthria (NIHSS 1, GCS 15). Initial non-contrast CT head was normal, excluding hemorrhage. CT angiography confirmed the diagnosis of distal basilar artery occlusion with cerebral perfusion deficit of the right superior cerebellar artery. She underwent successful mechanical thrombectomy within one hour of symptom onset with heparin restarted post-procedure. Post-procedure CTA demonstrated widely patent basilar artery without residual embolus. She experienced transient visual hallucinations and dizziness post-procedure (with insight preserved) that resolved during hospitalization, and she returned to baseline neurological status (no deficits on examination) prior to discharge a few days later. Long-term management included resumption of rivaroxaban and high-intensity statin therapy.
